title: Strict 550 nm Quarter-Wave Initialization with Expanded Search
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing all layer pairs at strict quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 550 nm (visible stopband center) with expanded thickness bounds and increased optimization evaluations will escape the local minimum observed in iteration_06 and recover or exceed the iteration_01 target score.
design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at stopband center wavelength maximizes reflectance in the stopband; optimization refines thicknesses to maintain high visible reflectance while recovering telecom transmittance.
proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate, air incidence. Layer 1 (adjacent to air): HfO2. Layer 20 (adjacent to substrate): SiO2. Exact count: 20 finite layers, 10 HfO2/SiO2 pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total thickness within manufacturable range
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses should remain above 30 nm for deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 material pair is industry-standard for space optics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector theory: maximum stopband reflectance when optical thickness = λ_center/4 for each layer
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Strict 550 nm initialization places optimizer in visible stopband basin
Expanded bounds allow thickness exploration beyond iteration_06 local minimum
Multi-start strategy reduces risk of stagnation
known_risks: Quarter-wave at 550 nm may degrade telecom transmittance if not properly optimized
20 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous dual-band performance
Optimizer may still converge to similar local minimum despite re-initialization
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternate HfO2 and SiO2 starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize all odd layers (HfO2) at thickness = 550/(4*n_HfO2) nm and all even layers (SiO2) at thickness = 550/(4*n_SiO2) nm using material registry refractive indices at 550 nm. Optimization bounds: each layer thickness ±40% from initialization value. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with max_evaluations = 5000, multi_start_count = 20. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (average transmittance 1530-1565 nm) and (average reflectance 400-700 nm) with equal weights. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
revision_reason: Iteration_06 showed score degradation from 0.8497 to 0.6163, indicating optimizer stagnation in local minimum. Feedback directive specifies strict 550 nm quarter-wave initialization with expanded bounds and increased evaluations to escape current spectral basin.
